title: Supported products and Cartier interchange on ordinary etale sites
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme on which a prime $\ell$ is invertible, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Work on small etale sites with roots-of-unity twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist, lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Write $H_C^a(X,\Lambda(b))$ for the cohomology of the derived functor of sections vanishing off a closed subset $C$ [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections]. There are natural associative bilinear products
$$H_C^a(X,\Lambda(b))\otimes H_D^{a'}(X,\Lambda(b'))\to H_{C\cap D}^{a+a'}(X,\Lambda(b+b'))$$
with sign $(-1)^{aa'}$ on interchange. For nested closed supports $Z\subset Y\subset X$ there are associative action products $H_Z^a(Y,\Lambda(b))\otimes H_Y^{a'}(X,\Lambda(b'))\to H_Z^{a+a'}(X,\Lambda(b+b'))$, satisfying the projection formula for classes on $Y$. Under the supported-Hom identification [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] these action products are composition of supported morphisms; after adjunction they are exceptional composition. These products commute with pullback of pairs, open restriction, and coefficient reduction.
For a line bundle $L$ with a trivialization $s$ off $C$, let $e_C(L,s)$ be the supported Kummer first Chern class [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology, lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. For two such pairs, with their supports enlarged to a common closed set when necessary,
$$e(L\otimes M,s\otimes t)=e(L,s)+e(M,t),\qquad e(L^\vee,s^\vee)=-e(L,s).$$
For an effective Cartier divisor $D$, $e_D(\mathcal O_X(D),1)$ is the class of $c_{D,\Lambda}$ in [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], whereas $e_D(\mathcal I_D,1)$ is its negative [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. A pseudo-divisor class defines an operator $G_{L,s}:H^a(C,\Lambda(b))\to H_C^{a+2}(X,\Lambda(b+1))$ by this action. For every closed $W\subset C$, the same nested action extends it to $G_{L,s}:H_W^a(C,\Lambda(b))\to H_W^{a+2}(X,\Lambda(b+1))$; this extension is used in iterated operators below, so both Cartier composites have domain $H^a(D_1\cap D_2,\Lambda(b))$ and codomain $H_{D_1\cap D_2}^{a+4}(X,\Lambda(b+2))$. Its restriction to $C$ is multiplication by $c_1(L|_C)$. For a class $x\in H^a(X,\Lambda(b))$, the image of $G_{L,s}(x|_C)$ in $H^{a+2}(X,\Lambda(b+1))$ after forgetting the support is $x\cdot c_1(L)$. If two effective Cartier divisors $D_1,D_2$ meet transversely, meaning each restricts to an effective Cartier divisor on the other, their ideal-normalized operators obey
$$G_{D_1\subset X}\,G_{D_1\cap D_2\subset D_1}=G_{D_2\subset X}\,G_{D_1\cap D_2\subset D_2}.$$
The equality uses the canonical identification of the intersections and twists; both operators use $e(\mathcal I_D,1)$. No regularity of $X$ is required.

source.place: Expose XVI, section 2.1 (pseudo-divisors), Lemma 2.2.2.4; supported pairings in Proposition 2.2.3.2 and proof of Theorem 2.3.2, pp. 235-236 (associativity and transverse Cartier interchange).

proof.text:
For a closed $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ put $P_C=i_*\Lambda_C$ in degree zero and $A_b=\Lambda_X(b)$. Apply [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] with its first support equal to $X$: the derived support complex is the homotopy fibre of restriction to $X-C$. By [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] this is $R\operatorname{Hom}_X(P_C,-)$. Module sheaves have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Taking cohomology and [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof] identify
$$H_C^a(X,A_b)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X,\Lambda)}(P_C,A_b[a]).$$
Use the natural normalization of [lem-asd-supported-kummer-support-hom-naturality]: pullback is inverse image followed by the inverse closed-constant exchange, and forgetting support is precomposition by $q_C:\Lambda_X\to P_C$. The twists $A_b$ are invertible flat degree-zero sheaves, with natural multiplication $A_b\otimes A_{b'}\cong A_{b+b'}$, by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. All ensuing formulas concern these ordinary small-etale Hom groups.

source.place: XVI 2.1, supported morphism representing a pseudo-divisor; Stacks 0A45, support triangle; derived-Hom interpretation

proof.text:
For each closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$, [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization] gives exact fully faithful module direct image and invertible counit $i^{-1}i_*\cong1$, with essential image the modules vanishing off $C$. Exact inverse image is [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Localizing this exact adjunction [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] retains its termwise counit, hence $i_*$ is fully faithful on derived categories too. Moreover, for a complex $K$ with cohomology supported on $C$, the unit $K\to i_*i^{-1}K$ is an isomorphism: its cohomology maps are the invertible supported units of the cited localization lemma. In particular
$$P_C\otimes^L A_b\cong i_*\Lambda_C(b).$$
Indeed tensor with the flat line $A_b$ is exact, its restriction off $C$ is zero, and applying $i^{-1}$ gives $\Lambda_C(b)$ under [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] and [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. This specifies the comparison by its restriction to $C$.

source.place: Tag 04CA, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward; module form Tag 08M3, lemma-i-star-equivalence; exact-adjunction localization Tag 015F

proof.text:
For closed $C,D$ and $I=C\times_XD$, use the specified flat-source isomorphism $\mu_{C,D}:P_C\otimes^LP_D\xrightarrow{\sim}P_I$ of [lem-pur-etale-closed-constant-tensor]. For representatives $\alpha:P_C\to A_b[a]$ and $\beta:P_D\to A_{b'}[a']$, define
$$\alpha\cup\beta=(A_b\otimes A_{b'}\cong A_{b+b'})[a+a']\circ t_{a,a'}(\alpha\otimes^L\beta)\circ\mu_{C,D}^{-1}.$$
Here $t$ is the shift comparison in [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus]. Its source flatness is supplied by the closed-constant tensor lemma, and the twist multiplication is [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Step 1 gives precisely the group and support claimed in the statement.

source.place: Tags 0FPL/0FPM, associative and symmetric cup diagrams; ordinary supported tensor-morphism construction using Tag 03Q1

proof.text: The tensor-morphism operation of [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus] is additive separately, associative, and changes by $(-1)^{aa'}$ under interchange. The source identifications $\mu$ obey exactly the same associativity and symmetry diagrams by [lem-pur-etale-closed-constant-tensor]. Twist multiplication is associative, and it is symmetric: by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] the twists are locally free of rank one, etale locally generated by $\zeta^{\otimes b}$ for a primitive root $\zeta$ (dual bases for negative twists), and the interchange of tensor factors fixes $\zeta^{\otimes b}\otimes\zeta^{\otimes b'}$, so twist multiplication commutes with the symmetry without sign. Substituting these three equalities in Step 3 proves bilinearity, associativity and the stated sign. No boundedness of a tensor of arbitrary complexes is used: the final coefficients here are the flat lines $A_{b+b'}$.

source.place: Tags 0FPL and 0FPM; substitution of signed tensor and closed-coefficient coherence

proof.text: For a morphism $v:X'\to X$ use the normalized supported-Hom pullback of [lem-asd-supported-kummer-support-hom-naturality]. The exchange maps $v^{-1}P_C\cong P_{C'}$ preserve $\mu$ by [lem-pur-etale-closed-constant-tensor]. Exactness of inverse image and the pullback identity for shifted tensor morphisms in [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus], together with the twist identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], identify the inverse image of every factor in Step 3 with its primed factor. Hence $v^*(\alpha\cup\beta)=v^*\alpha\cup v^*\beta$. This includes open restriction and respects the actual support-forgetting maps by Step 1.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; supported functoriality as in cohomology.tex Tag 0G78, with etale closed-coefficient exchange

proof.text: Let $N\geq n$ and let $T=-\otimes^L_{\Lambda_N}\Lambda_n$ on the same etale site [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The canonical source comparison $T(P_{C,N})\cong P_{C,n}$ preserves $q_C$ by [lem-asd-supported-kummer-scalar-source]. The power map on roots of unity gives $T(\Lambda_N(b))\cong\Lambda_n(b)$: etale locally choose a primitive $\ell^N$-th root, whose image is a primitive $\ell^n$-th root, so the map sends a basis to a basis; use tensor powers and dual bases for all signed twists [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The functor $T$ is symmetric strong monoidal with its canonical comparisons by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] (the underlying topos map is the identity). On flat degree-zero $P_C,P_D$, its comparison carries $\mu_{C,D}$ to the reduced $\mu$: both multiply the reduced local sections. The shifted comparison has the same scalar $(-1)^{a'p}$ on total K-flat models, since scalar extension preserves these integer signs. Thus applying $T$ to Step 3 proves product reduction compatibility, without assuming that reduction is exact.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 0D6D; derived scalar extension and closed coefficient source; roots-of-unity power comparison

proof.text:
For $Z\xrightarrow{k}Y\xrightarrow{i}X$, represent $\alpha\in H_Z^a(Y,\Lambda(b))$ by $k_*\Lambda_Z\to\Lambda_Y(b)[a]$ and $\beta\in H_Y^{a'}(X,\Lambda(b'))$ by $P_Y\to A_{b'}[a']$. Define
$$\alpha\star\beta=\beta(b)[a]\circ i_*\alpha:P_Z\longrightarrow A_{b+b'}[a+a'].$$
The intermediate target is $P_Y(b)[a]$ by Step 2; direct images compose because both section functors evaluate a sheaf on the same fibre product, and their derived functors are termwise exact by [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization]. This construction is additive in each class. For a third nested support, both parenthesizations are the same three morphisms in the same order with the same twist-shift additions, so composition proves associativity.

source.place: XVI 2.1, composition of supported morphisms; 2.2.3.2, canonical action of cohomology of the support

proof.text:
For an ordinary class $u:\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_Y(t)[p]$ and a supported class $\alpha:k_*\Lambda_Z\to\Lambda_Y(b)[a]$, the cup $u\cup\alpha$ equals $u(b)[a]\circ\alpha$. To see this, insert the tensor-unit inverse in the cup formula, factor $u\otimes\alpha$ as $(u\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes\alpha)$, and use naturality of the left unitor and $t_{0,a}$ (with first target $\Lambda_Y(t)[p]$) of [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus]. Therefore
$$(u\cup\alpha)\star\beta=\alpha\star(u\star\beta).$$
Both sides are $\beta(b+t)[a+p]\circ i_*u(b)[a]\circ i_*\alpha$. This is the projection formula for the action of classes on $Y$. Writing the class $u$ on the other side introduces exactly the Koszul sign from Step 4.

source.place: XVI 2.2.3.2, cohomology-on-support action; formal tensor-unit and composition calculation

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], a closed $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ is proper and finite type. Since $X$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $Y$ Noetherian. The compactification with identity open and proper map $i$ is a compactification between Noetherian schemes. Thus [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] supplies $i_*=Ri_*\dashv i^!$ with counit $\epsilon_i$. If $\bar\alpha:\Lambda_Z\to k^!\Lambda_Y(b)[a]$ and $\bar\beta:\Lambda_Y\to i^!\Lambda_X(b')[a']$ are the transposes of $\alpha,\beta$, the transpose of Step 7's composite is
$$k^!(\bar\beta)(b)[a]\circ\bar\alpha.$$
Indeed untransposing gives $\epsilon_i\circ i_*\bar\beta\circ i_*\epsilon_k\circ i_*k_*\bar\alpha$, with the indicated twist-shifts. Naturality of $\epsilon_k$ rewrites this as the untranspose under the pasted counit for $(ik)^!\cong k^!i^!$ of [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition]. Twists commute with these adjoints because they are invertible lines: moving a line across Hom uses its dual and Step 2's twist projection identification. Thus this is exceptional composition of the actual supported morphisms, with no purity identification asserted.

source.place: XVI 2.1 and 2.3.2, reading supported composition through exceptional adjunction

proof.text: The nested action also has the asserted functoriality. For pullback, the canonical exchange $v^{-1}i_*K\to i'_*v_Y^{-1}K$ is an isomorphism for a closed $i$: both objects are supported on $Y'$, and restriction to $Y'$ gives the identity by the counits in [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization], exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and the composition comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Step 2's supported derived-unit test proves the claim, including naturality on morphisms. The identical argument gives the scalar comparison $T_Xi_*K\cong i_*T_YK$: restriction commutes with scalar extension by composition of ringed pullbacks, and open restriction of $T_Xi_*K$ is zero by that same comparison. Consequently both pullback and reduction preserve the composition in Step 7. On closed constant sources the scalar comparison is the unit-normalized one of [lem-asd-supported-kummer-scalar-source], and on twist targets it is that of Step 6. Open restriction is a pullback case.

source.place: Tags 04CA and 0D6D; closed supported-unit test and composition of ringed pullbacks

proof.text: Put $U=X-C$. The frame torsor of a trivialized line $(L,s)$ is a $\mathbf G_m$-torsor with specified section on $U$, by [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor]. Its relative class $[L,s]\in H^1(X,U;\mathbf G_m)$ is [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology]. Apply its relative connecting homomorphism for the exact Kummer sequence [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] with exponent $\ell^n$ and define $e_C(L,s)=\delta[L,s]$. The relative groups of [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] use abelian-sheaf cohomology, Step 1 uses $\Lambda$-module cohomology of $\Lambda(1)=\mu_{\ell^n}$; they agree canonically. Take an injective resolution $\mu_{\ell^n}\to I$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules. Restriction to $U$, i.e. to the slice $X_{\mathrm{et}}/U\simeq U_{\mathrm{et}}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-over-open], has the exact left adjoint extension by zero [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-injectives], which carries the $\Lambda$-action; so $I|_U$ is an injective resolution of $\Lambda_U$-modules. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget] on $X$ and on $U$ these terms are acyclic as abelian sheaves. Hence the one complex $\operatorname{Cone}(\Gamma(X,I)\to\Gamma(U,I))[-1]$ computes both the abelian relative group and the support complex of Step 1, so $\delta[L,s]$ is the required class in $H^2_C(X,\Lambda(1))$. Naturality of the relative connecting maps proves pullback and support-forgetting compatibility. For reduction $N\to n$ the Kummer square has vertical maps $z\mapsto z^{\ell^{N-n}}$ on the kernel and on the first $\mathbf G_m$, and identity on the last $\mathbf G_m$; the square commutes since $\ell^n\ell^{N-n}=\ell^N$. Its relative connecting square proves the stated power-map reduction for $e$.

source.place: XVI 2.1, supported first Chern class; Stacks 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1, relative refinement; 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence

proof.text: Enlarge the supports to their union, so both trivializations are on the same open $U$. The frame torsor of $(L\otimes M,s\otimes t)$ is the contracted product of the two frame torsors [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor]. Their relative classes add: apply naturality in [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] first to the two projections $\mathbf G_m^2\to\mathbf G_m$, identifying the class of the product torsor with $([L,s],[M,t])$, and then to multiplication $\mathbf G_m^2\to\mathbf G_m$. Relative cohomology preserves finite products, since finite sums of injective resolutions compute the product and its restriction cone componentwise. Multiplication therefore induces addition. The connecting map is additive, so $e(L\otimes M,s\otimes t)=e(L,s)+e(M,t)$. Taking $(M,t)=(L^\vee,s^\vee)$ gives $e(L^\vee,s^\vee)=-e(L,s)$, since the trivial pair has zero relative torsor class.

source.place: XVI 2.1 and proof of 2.3.2, p.236, additivity for trivialized line bundles

proof.text: For an effective Cartier divisor $D$, [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] identifies $e_D(\mathcal O_X(D),1)$ with the morphism $c_{D,\Lambda}$, and identifies its support-forgetting image with $+c_1(\mathcal O_X(D))$. Since $\mathcal O_X(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], Step 12 gives $e_D(\mathcal I_D,1)=-[c_{D,\Lambda}]$. This is the ideal normalization in XVI Definition 2.1.1, not a sign convention chosen after the composition calculation. The pullback of these trivialized lines when the pulled divisor is Cartier is [lem-asd-supported-kummer-cartier-pullback]; the same holds for their duals, by tensoring the evaluation pairing.

source.place: XVI Definition 2.1.1 and its warning on the ideal/divisor signs; Stacks 0C4U, lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-divisors

proof.text:
Let $i:C\hookrightarrow X$, and let $e:P_C\to A_1[2]$ represent $e_C(L,s)$. For $u:\Lambda_C\to\Lambda_C(b)[a]$, define
$$G_{L,s}(u)=e(b)[a]\circ i_*u.$$
More generally, for $W\subset C$ closed and $u\in H_W^a(C,\Lambda(b))$, the identical formula with source $P_W$ is $u\star e\in H_W^{a+2}(X,\Lambda(b+1))$. These are well typed by Steps 2 and 7. Pulling the first formula back to $C$ gives the cup with $i^{-1}e$ by Step 8. By [lem-asd-supported-kummer-support-hom-naturality] and Step 11, $i^{-1}e$ is $c_1(L|_C)$: pullback to $C$ of forgetting support commutes, and the pulled trivialized open is empty. Thus restriction of $G$ is multiplication by $c_1(L|_C)$, as in XVI Lemma 2.2.2.4.

source.place: XVI 2.1 and Lemma 2.2.2.4; explicit extension to smaller supports by nested action

proof.text:
Let $x:\Lambda_X\to A_b[a]$. Naturality of the closed adjunction unit gives $i_*i^{-1}x\circ q_C=q_C(b)[a]\circ x$. Consequently forgetting support in Step 14 yields
$$G_{L,s}(x|_C)\circ q_C=e(b)[a]\circ q_C(b)[a]\circ x=c_1(L)(b)[a]\circ x=c_1(L)\cup x.$$
Here $e\circ q_C=c_1(L)$ is Step 11 and the last equality is the tensor-unit factorization of Step 8, with support all of $X$. Since $c_1(L)$ has degree two, it also equals $x\cup c_1(L)$ by the sign formula of [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus]. This proves the requested support-forgetting identity with its prescribed sign.

source.place: XVI 2.1, forgetting the support of a pseudo-divisor class; tensor-unit projection calculation

proof.text:
Put $I=D_1\times_XD_2$ and $i_j:D_j\hookrightarrow X$. Let $e_j=e_{D_j}(\mathcal I_{D_j},1)$. Transversality makes $I\hookrightarrow D_1$ an effective Cartier divisor, and Step 13 together with [lem-asd-supported-kummer-support-hom-naturality] identifies $i_1^{-1}e_2$ with its ideal-normalized class $e_{I\subset D_1}$. In particular the comparison of ideal lines and their trivializations is justified by [lem-asd-supported-kummer-cartier-pullback], taking duals. Under $P_{D_1}\otimes^LP_{D_2}\cong P_I$ of [lem-pur-etale-closed-constant-tensor], one has
$$i_{1*}e_{I\subset D_1}=1_{P_{D_1}}\otimes^Le_2:P_I\to P_{D_1}(1)[2].$$
Both endpoints are in the fully faithful closed derived image of Step 2, and restricting this equality to $D_1$ gives the just-proved pullback identity. Thus this equality holds globally in the derived category; it is not inferred by gluing arbitrary local derived morphisms.

source.place: XVI proof of Theorem 2.3.2, p.236, transverse Cartier interchange; derived tensor proof using Cartier pullback rather than the external Fujiwara reference

proof.text: For $u\in H^a(I,\Lambda(b))$, Step 16 and tensor bifunctoriality identify the morphism underlying $G_{D_1\subset X}G_{I\subset D_1}$ with $e_1\cup e_2:P_I\to\Lambda_X(2)[4]$, followed on the source by the supported action of $u$. Indeed its two arrows are $1\otimes e_2$ and $e_1\otimes1$ with the shifts moved out; their composite is $e_1\otimes e_2$. With $D_1,D_2$ exchanged the same calculation gives $e_2\cup e_1$. By [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus] the interchange sign is $(-1)^{2\cdot2}=1$, and [lem-pur-etale-closed-constant-tensor] identifies the two intersection sources canonically. Therefore the two operators agree in $H_I^{a+4}(X,\Lambda(b+2))$ for every $u$. Every construction used above is natural for pullback and reduction by Steps 5, 6, 10 and 11, hence so are these operators and identities. Regularity of $X$ was never used.

source.place: XVI proof of Theorem 2.3.2, p.236, equality of transverse Cartier operators; even-degree tensor interchange

split_report.summary: Seventeen explicit ordinary-etale steps: supported Hom, exact closed image and twists, signed tensor cup products, pullback and derived coefficient reduction, nested composition and projection, exceptional transposes, additive relative Kummer classes, ideal sign, smaller-support Gysin action and transverse Cartier interchange. No new nodes. Corrected the omitted smaller-support domain of iterated G operators; no hypothesis or asserted equality was removed. All cited statements were opened; the field-specific pro-etale cup nodes are not used for the general Noetherian base.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q20-460794973 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, all 17 steps, and the statements of all 25 cited nodes. Source checked: ILO XVI 2.1/Def 2.1.1 (pp.228-229, including the warning that I and Z have opposite classes), Lemma 2.2.2.4, Prop 2.2.3.2 and the proof of Thm 2.3.2 (pp.235-237). The statement correction is faithful and needed for the types: in ILO's Fujiwara interchange the outer Gys acts on a class supported on P'. The added twist stmt_dep covers negative twists. No hypothesis is added or weakened, and the citers still hold. Steps 1-10, 12-14, 16 and 17 are correct. I recomputed the shift and Koszul signs: t_{p,a} on a degree-0 class gives sign +1; Step 17 has (-1)^4=1. The ideal sign (I,1)^vee=(O(D),s_D) gives e(I,1)=-c_D. Step 16's equality i_{1*}e_{I subset D1}=1 tensor e_2 holds globally because the closed derived image is fully faithful. Fault repaired (C1/E6): Step 11 identified the abelian-sheaf relative torsor group H^2(X,U;mu) with Step 1's Lambda-module H^2_C(X,Lambda(1)) without argument. It now cites lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget, lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-injectives and lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-over-open: a Lambda-injective resolution restricts to a Lambda_U-injective one and is acyclic as abelian sheaves, so one cone computes both groups. All three are on route, reviewed, create no cycle, and are already in the batch-5 closure. Wording fixes: Step 4 now gives the local-generator reason that twist multiplication is symmetric. Step 15 now writes c_1 cup x, with the ordinary class on the left as in Step 8; the result is unchanged because the degree is even. Batch 5: the closure from both targets, computed with and without the item's proof_deps, differs by 0 nodes. lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization (generic closed subtopos and module i_* exactness) and closed-constant-tensor and scalar-source (both reach only lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar, i.e. stalk of a tensor) are generic and outside both assumptions, so accepted. Route: the 3 off-route tools (that trf node, kun-inverse-image-monoidal, sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons) are generic and accepted. No SGA. Not a duplicate of the pur/pod supported-cup nodes, which are over a field, pro-etale or smooth only. No new nodes.
